Introduction · 15 min
A Question of Singularity
3h 30min6 playersRingworld RPG 1984
Read Aloud — Opening
The Foolish Endeavour dropped from hyperdrive six hours ago and has been holding position since. The Ringworld fills the forward viewport — not as a planet but as a wall, a horizon that curves upward in both directions and never ends. From this distance you can make out the shadow squares drifting in their slow procession, and the faint smear of weather systems moving across a surface the size of a million Earths. You have all seen it before. It still does not feel normal. Chief Navigator Talren has not left the instruments since arrival. He keeps rechecking the same figures. Captain Vorn has twice asked him if there is an error. Both times, Talren has said the same thing: "There is no error. That is the problem." The anomaly is there on every screen. A circular region approximately forty kilometres in diameter on the Ringworld's inner surface. Weather systems stop at its edge as if hitting a wall. Gravitational readings within the boundary are not elevated — they are absent. A perfect, engineered nothing. And at its centre: a gravitational signature that your instruments say should not be physically possible at this scale. Brakk has already checked the weapons systems twice. The landing team is ready.
Pre-Mission — Establish Before Descent
· Ship maintains orbit and keeps comms open · Vorn's standing order: observe, do not interfere with Ringworld systems · Talren's private concern: the mass signature is growing, slowly but measurably · Brakk's position: any unknown Ringworld mechanism should be assumed hostile until proven otherwise
GM — Tone
Procedural unease, not horror yet. The wrongness should feel intellectual before it feels visceral. Music: long, low drones — ambient, not melodic. Gradually dim lighting as they descend. By Act Three, lighting should feel slightly wrong — not dark, just slightly too even.
Act One · The Surface
The Boundary
AwarenessScience (Physics)
Description
A perfectly circular line where the Ringworld's surface ecology simply stops. Grass, dust, insects — everything halts at a boundary with no physical marker. On one side: normal Ringworld. On the other: stillness. The air pressure is slightly different. Sound carries oddly — echoes arrive before they should.
GM — Atmosphere
Like crossing a threshold in a building with no door. The wrongness is in the physics. Instruments flicker within 10 metres of the line, then stabilise. Biological functions feel subtly out of sync for ~30 seconds after crossing, then normalise. The abandoned comm unit in the zone still has power — when activated, it plays a recording of this conversation. Not exactly. Close enough to be wrong.

Act One · The Surface
Quiet Zone — Open Ground
Clue 1 EssentialClue 4 OptionalAwarenessScience (Survey)
Description
Flat, grey-brown ground. No plants, no insects, no wind. The sky is normal above — but weather stops at the boundary edge. Clouds pile up against invisible walls. Ground shows tracks — many sets, overlapping, some going in impossible directions. Equipment scattered: a survey pack, a comm unit, a single boot. None damaged. All cold.
GM — Absolute Silence
Only the players' own sounds. They will feel watched, though nothing watching is visible. The comm unit found in the equipment: when activated it plays back a recording of this conversation. Not exactly. Close enough to be wrong. Use this deliberately — the first confirmed echo.

Act One · The Surface
Marr's Camp
Clue 2 EssentialResearch
Description
A rough shelter from salvaged materials — hull plating, wire, torn thermal blanket. Inside: a cot, hundreds of identical notebooks (handwriting growing erratic toward end of each, resetting to neat script at start of the next), and an autodoc with nearly exhausted power. The first entry in every single notebook reads: "Day one. The Endeavour has arrived. Earlier than last time."
GM — The Notebooks
Later notebooks contain information that hasn't happened yet in this iteration. One entry reads: "The tall one with the grey jacket goes to the arch first. Don't let them." Marr is not mad. He is exhausted. Everything he knows, he will tell. The tragedy is that knowing everything has not been enough.

Act One · The Surface
The Transit Arch
Clue 3 OptionalElectronicsAwareness Hard
Description
A standard Ringworld stepping-disc transit arch — but behaving impossibly. Activates intermittently with no trigger. When it activates, it produces objects: tools, equipment fragments, once a human hand (which disappears before retrieval). The destination display cycles through coordinates that do not resolve to any known location.
GM — The Arch
The arch cycles through outputs of previous iterations — physical matter briefly surfacing before the loop reclaims it. Marr refuses to go near it. "The last time I touched it, I woke up at the beginning." One of the tools bears an engraving matching equipment of one of the player characters. Hold this moment before you describe it.

Marr says directly: "We need to go to the Spire. The answers are there and we are running out of time before it resets again. I can feel it." Move immediately.
Act Two · The Spire
The Weather Spire — Exterior
Science (Engineering)
Description
~200 metres tall. Perfectly circular. Scrith construction — faint iridescence of near-indestructible material. A single entry point, open. No door. The opening pulses with light that is not quite any colour the players have a name for. At the base, scratched into the scrith (which should be unscratchable — this alone is remarkable): hundreds of tally marks. Marr's work. "I stopped counting," he says.
GM — Scale
The Spire has presence in the way that very old, very large things have presence. It is not threatening. It simply exists, and the players are very small next to it. Let that settle before anything else happens.

Act Two · The Spire
Control Level
Clue 6 EssentialClue 8 OptionalComputer 75%Science (Physics) Hard
Description
A circular chamber, walls covered in read-out surfaces — not screens, but surfaces that shift and reconfigure showing data in formats requiring Science rolls to partially parse. A raised dais at centre with a smooth hemisphere interface that responds to touch. The room hums at a frequency felt more in the chest than heard.
GM — The Interface
Working in here feels like standing inside something's thought process. The interface responds to biological contact and displays targeted information drawn from the system's understanding of that individual. What it shows is not always welcome. In Act Two the loops start tightening. Use something that actually happened at the table — repeat it back slightly differently. This is more effective than any written text.

Act Two · The Spire
Log Chamber
Clue 5 EssentialClue 7 OptionalLinguistics + Computer
Description
A smaller room Marr knows but players would not find without him (or a Hard Awareness roll). Contains the system's actual iteration record — not in any language, but translatable through Computer + Linguistics + Science (Physics). The logs go back three hundred years.
GM — The Critical Line
If players cannot translate the logs, Marr knows the key entries by heart. He recites the critical line from memory, quietly, while staring at the wall: "Conscious variable introduced. That's us. That's always been us." This is the emotional centre of the scenario. Let it land.

Fast Track at 2:45
The same five seconds of a player speaking replay three times in a row, audible to everyone. Marr says, with zero drama: "It's accelerating. We need to go down. Now." Move immediately to the descent.
Act Three · The Core
The Descent
CON × 5
Description
A shaft in the floor of the Spire's lowest level — 3 metres in diameter, handholds descending into darkness. Gravity normal until ~50 metres down, then fluctuates. Not dangerously — but weight changes are perceptible. The descent takes ~10 minutes. Loops manifest visually for the first time. Players may see echoes of themselves — half-visible figures descending in slightly different configurations, making slightly different choices. These echoes do not interact. They are simply there.
GM — Marr Stays
Marr will not descend. He has been here before. He stays at the top of the shaft and tells them: "Someone always goes in. No one has come back wrong. But the loop always resets after. I don't know if it's because you fail, or because you succeed." This line should hang in the air. Then they go down.

Act Three · The Core — 30 min max
The Core Chamber
Clue 9Clue 10Science (Mathematics) HardAwareness Hard
STABILITY REQUIRED
VARIABLES INTERFERE
RESOLUTION PENDING
Description
A spherical chamber, 40 metres in diameter. Walls are scrith — but here, transparent. Through it: the Ringworld's superstructure, and beyond that, the void. At the exact centre, suspended by nothing visible: the singularity. The size of a human fist. It warps light around it. Looking directly at it feels like trying to read text that keeps moving. Time feels different here — not slowed, but less certain.
THE SYSTEM
Ringworld Structural Management · Non-conscious · 300-year operation
Not an enemy. A machine solving a problem. It does not know the players are there in any way that matters to it. The horror is not malice — it is indifference operating at Ringworld scale.

GM — Forcing the Decision
At 3:10 if still deliberating: singularity begins audibly resonating — tone increasing in pitch. Vorn's comms cut out. The loops stop entirely. The system is no longer iterating. It is converging. Marr's voice from above: "Last time someone did nothing, I woke up here again. I don't want to wake up here again."
Art Direction
When you show the core image, let it sit before you describe the scene. Silence, then the image, then: "This is what you see." Give it room. The silence is part of the reveal.
Epilogue · 15 min
Outcomes
Full Success
Players provide sufficient data OR address the mass discrepancy source
System completes a clean iteration. The singularity dissipates. The quiet zone normalises over ~1 hour. Marr is released from the loop. The Foolish Endeavour receives one clear signal: RESOLUTION COMPLETE.
Partial Success
All conscious variables withdraw and maintain distance
System completes an iteration, incompletely. Quiet zone remains. Singularity does not grow. Marr leaves with the players — but not certain the loop is over. Anomaly listed as contained, unresolved.
Pyrrhic
Players allow the system to complete without intervention
Singularity becomes self-sustaining. Region lost — permanent anomaly. Ship barely breaks orbit. Marr, who stayed at the shaft head, is not seen again. A discovery that reshapes Known Space cosmology. One man unaccounted for.
Failure / Reset
Unable to decide, or direct attack on the core
Loop reset triggers. Players wake at Introduction with fragmented memories. Each player loses 1D6 PP. Option: run compressed Act One with partial memories, ending with a harder choice.
Read Aloud — Full Success Closing
The tone drops. Not gradually — it simply stops, between one moment and the next. The chamber walls clear. Through the scrith, the Ringworld's superstructure is visible again — solid, exact, enormous, exactly as it should be. Where the singularity was, there is nothing. Not a void. Just the air of the chamber, and the faint hum of a system returning to its normal operational state. When you surface from the shaft, Marr is sitting on the floor of the Spire, back against the wall, eyes closed. He opens them when he hears you. For a moment he says nothing. Then: "It's quiet. The right kind of quiet." The Foolish Endeavour's comms reconnect. Vorn's voice: "What happened down there?" You realise you are going to have to explain this. You are not sure you can.

Key Skills
Science (Physics) 78% · Research 82% · Awareness 70% · Computer 60% · Science (Engineering) 65% · Linguistics 55%
Motivation
Wants out of the region. Will not leave without making sure someone understands what they're dealing with — because the last three times he tried to simply run, the loop reset before he reached the boundary.
Knows
Region resets on event-trigger (approach core, fail to resolve). Each reset leaves mass residue. System responds to input. The Spire is the access point. Logs are readable — barely. Has tried 14 approaches. None worked.
Disposition
Terrified but controlled. Will help because the players are his best chance. Will not perform heroics. If things deteriorate, first instinct is to run — and he will need to be talked back.
LOOP MEMORY — Marr retains partial memory across iterations. The GM may give him information about player actions that "haven't happened yet" in this loop, delivered as fragmentary warnings or apparent non-sequiturs.
Ship Crew — Comms Only
Foolish Endeavour · Three Voices
Captain Vorn — Withdrawal
Controlled, military-trained, increasingly strained. Wants everyone off the Ringworld. Will issue direct withdrawal order in Act Three. Pilot 85% · Command 78% · Persuade 72%
Talren — Engagement
Rapid, excited, terrified underneath. Has not slept. Dangerously enthusiastic. Will push players toward deeper investigation without considering consequences. Science (Physics) 88% · Science (Mathematics) 82% · Computer 79%
Brakk — Destruction
Flat, deliberate. Economy of words. Solution: shut it down by any means. Knows force won't help but will advocate for it loudly. Ranged Weapon 82% · Unarmed 75%
USE THEM: Vorn = withdrawal pressure · Talren = reckless engagement · Brakk = blunt destruction. Their escalating disagreements over comms mirror the players' own debate.

Session Outcomes
Full Success
Provide sufficient data OR address the mass discrepancy source
System completes a clean iteration. Singularity dissipates. Quiet zone normalises over ~1 hour. Marr released from the loop. Foolish Endeavour receives: RESOLUTION COMPLETE.
Partial Success
All conscious variables withdraw and maintain distance
System completes an iteration, incompletely. Quiet zone remains. Singularity stable, not growing. Marr leaves with the players — not certain the loop is over. Anomaly: contained, unresolved.
Pyrrhic
Allow the system to complete without intervention
Singularity becomes self-sustaining. Region lost — permanent anomaly. Ship barely breaks orbit. Marr stays. Greatest scientific discovery in Known Space history. One man unaccounted for.
Failure / Reset
Unable to decide, or direct attack on the core
Loop reset. Imperfect. Players wake at Introduction with fragmented memories. 1D6 PP loss each. Option: run compressed Act One with partial memories, harder choice at the core.
GM — No Right Answer
All four outcomes are valid. Do not steer. Do not hint. Let them decide. Whatever they choose, it means something. The question the scenario poses is not about the physics — it is about what you do when you are the variable causing the problem.
